_nota: Piloto de canciones y chants. Una unidad por nivel en ingles y una en frances, para aprobar el estilo antes de escribir las 150. La letra sale del vocabulario y la gramatica de la propia unidad: no es una cancion generica con el titulo cambiado.

en/starters/01.gramatica: It is a… / What colour is…?

chant.estilo: playground chant for 6-year-olds, call and response, handclaps and foot stomps, one adult leader voice and a small chorus of children answering, spoken-sung, 92 BPM, no melody instruments, very clear consonants
chant.letra:
[Leader]
What colour is it? What colour is it?
[Kids]
Red! Red! The ball is red!

[Leader]
What colour is it? What colour is it?
[Kids]
Yellow! Yellow! The kite is yellow!

[Leader]
What colour is it? What colour is it?
[Kids]
Blue! Blue! The train is blue!

[Leader]
What colour is it? What colour is it?
[Kids]
Green! Green! The car is green!

[Leader]
One more time — everybody!
[Kids]
Red ball, yellow kite, blue train, green car!
It's my toy box! It's my toy box!

cancion.estilo: happy children's pop, ukulele, glockenspiel and handclaps, bright warm female voice with a small kids' chorus on the refrain, 104 BPM, simple and nursery-friendly, no heavy drums
cancion.letra:
[Verse 1]
Open the box and look inside,
there's a red ball ready to hide.
A yellow kite, a little blue train,
let's take them out and play again!

[Chorus]
It's a ball! It's a kite!
It's a train! It's a car!
What colour is it? What colour is it?
Tell me what you are!

[Verse 2]
Here's my teddy, soft and brown,
here's my doll with a yellow gown.
Green and red and blue and gold —
more than my two hands can hold!

[Chorus]
It's a ball! It's a kite!
It's a train! It's a car!
What colour is it? What colour is it?
Tell me what you are!

[Bridge — soft]
Who is hiding in the toy box?
A little bird with an orange beak…
Pip! Pip! Hello, Pip!

[Chorus — big finish]
It's a ball! It's a kite!
It's a train! It's a car!
What colour is it? What colour is it?
Tell me what you are!

en/movers/03.gramatica: past simple: went / saw / had / rode / won

chant.estilo: playground chant for 9-year-olds, call and response, claps on the off-beat and stomps, leader voice plus kids chorus, spoken-sung, 96 BPM, no melody instruments, punchy
chant.letra:
[Leader]
Today I go —
[Kids]
yesterday I WENT!

[Leader]
Today I see —
[Kids]
yesterday I SAW!

[Leader]
Today I have —
[Kids]
yesterday I HAD!

[Leader]
Today I ride —
[Kids]
yesterday I RODE!

[Leader]
Today I eat —
[Kids]
yesterday I ATE!

[Leader]
Today I win —
[Kids]
yesterday I WON!

[All]
Went, saw, had, rode, ate, won —
yesterday at the funfair, everyone!

cancion.estilo: upbeat children's indie-pop, acoustic guitar, tambourine, fairground organ in the chorus, bright mixed voices, 112 BPM, cheerful and story-like
cancion.letra:
[Verse 1]
Yesterday we went to the funfair,
yesterday we saw the big wheel turn.
Mateo had a ticket in his pocket —
he lost it twice, but he never learns!

[Chorus]
Went, saw, had —
yesterday, yesterday!
Rode, ate, won —
what a day, what a day!

[Verse 2]
Sofía rode the horses round and round,
Erik ate a hot dog on the way.
Valentina won a giant panda —
she couldn't even carry it away!

[Chorus]
Went, saw, had —
yesterday, yesterday!
Rode, ate, won —
what a day, what a day!

[Bridge]
Today is today and today we say GO,
but when it's finished we say WENT.
Today we SEE, and after that
we tell the story: yesterday we SAW.

[Chorus — final]
Went, saw, had —
yesterday, yesterday!
Rode, ate, won —
what a day, what a day!

chant.estilo: school-yard chant for 11-year-olds, body percussion, claps and desk taps, leader and chorus, spoken with attitude, 100 BPM, no melody instruments
chant.letra:
[Leader]
What have you got on Monday?
[Kids]
Maths, maths, we've got maths!

[Leader]
What have you got on Tuesday?
[Kids]
Science and art, science and art!

[Leader]
What have you got on Wednesday?
[Kids]
Music and history — clap your hands!

[Leader]
What have you got on Thursday?
[Kids]
Geography — where in the world?

[Leader]
What have you got on Friday?
[Kids]
SPORT! SPORT! Double sport!

[All]
Check the timetable, don't be late,
break at eleven, homework at eight!

cancion.estilo: energetic children's pop-rock, electric guitar, driving bass, claps, confident young mixed voices, 120 BPM, school-anthem feel
cancion.letra:
[Verse 1]
I get up early, I check the timetable,
maths before break and science after lunch.
I carry my books and I know where I'm going,
Friday is double sport — thanks a bunch!

[Chorus]
She studies history, he studies art,
we all do music on Wednesday.
Check the timetable, know it by heart —
this is my school day!

[Verse 2]
Diego finishes his homework on the bus,
Maya draws a map of every sea.
Oliver plays guitar in the music room,
and the bell goes at half past three.

[Chorus]
She studies history, he studies art,
we all do music on Wednesday.
Check the timetable, know it by heart —
this is my school day!

[Bridge — quieter]
I study. You study. He studies.
One little S when it's he, she or it —
and the whole week fits.

[Chorus — final]
She studies history, he studies art,
we all do music on Wednesday.
Check the timetable, know it by heart —
this is my school day!

fr/starters/01.gramatica: C'est un… / De quelle couleur est… ?

chant.estilo: comptine de cour de récréation pour enfants de 6 ans, question-réponse, claquements de mains et pieds, une voix d'adulte qui mène et un petit chœur d'enfants qui répond, parlé-chanté, 92 BPM, sans instruments mélodiques, articulation très nette, français de France
chant.letra:
[Meneur]
De quelle couleur ? De quelle couleur ?
[Enfants]
Rouge ! Rouge ! Le ballon est rouge !

[Meneur]
De quelle couleur ? De quelle couleur ?
[Enfants]
Jaune ! Jaune ! Le cerf-volant est jaune !

[Meneur]
De quelle couleur ? De quelle couleur ?
[Enfants]
Bleu ! Bleu ! Le train est bleu !

[Meneur]
De quelle couleur ? De quelle couleur ?
[Enfants]
Vert ! Vert ! La voiture est verte !

[Meneur]
Encore une fois — tout le monde !
[Enfants]
Ballon rouge, cerf-volant jaune, train bleu, voiture verte !
C'est ma boîte à jouets ! C'est ma boîte à jouets !

cancion.titulo: La boîte à jouets de Pip
cancion.estilo: chanson pour enfants joyeuse, ukulélé, glockenspiel et claquements de mains, voix féminine chaleureuse avec un petit chœur d'enfants au refrain, 104 BPM, simple et enfantine, français de France, sans grosse batterie
cancion.letra:
[Couplet 1]
Ouvre la boîte et regarde dedans,
un ballon rouge se cache dedans.
Un cerf-volant jaune, un petit train bleu,
sors-les vite, on joue tous les deux !

[Refrain]
C'est un ballon ! C'est un cerf-volant !
C'est un train ! C'est une voiture !
De quelle couleur ? De quelle couleur ?
Dis-le-moi, je t'assure !

[Couplet 2]
Voici mon nounours, tout doux, tout brun,
voici ma poupée en jaune et carmin.
Vert et rouge et bleu et doré —
mes deux mains ne peuvent pas tout porter !

[Refrain]
C'est un ballon ! C'est un cerf-volant !
C'est un train ! C'est une voiture !
De quelle couleur ? De quelle couleur ?
Dis-le-moi, je t'assure !

[Pont — doux]
Qui se cache dans la boîte à jouets ?
Un petit oiseau au bec orangé…
Pip ! Pip ! Bonjour, Pip !

[Refrain — final]
C'est un ballon ! C'est un cerf-volant !
C'est un train ! C'est une voiture !
De quelle couleur ? De quelle couleur ?
Dis-le-moi, je t'assure !

_aprobado.nota: La toma que el usuario marco con pulgar arriba el 2-sep-2026. El prompt de estilo de ese chant queda como formula: si otro chant no suena bien, comparar contra este.
